text:
Dmitry Orlov had the night of his season last weekend in Utah: a goal and three assists, including the third-period goal that gave San Jose its first lead, in a shootout win. San Jose Hockey Now wrote that he and Mason Marchment are finding their games. At 35, with a 2018 Cup, he is the veteran on a young blue line.

The scoring is solid for him. He has 3 goals and 14 points in 24 games, already matching last season's goal total, with 8 points on the power play, which is where Evolving-Hockey says most of his value came from last season. His shot still has real heat, top 13% of the league by speed.

Five on five is the problem. The Sharks get only about 41% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly four points worse than without him, and his minutes have dropped about two a night over the last ten games. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping entries at his blue line better than a typical defenseman last season. We'd watch whether that shows up again, because the power play alone can't carry his minutes.
